Hi John,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we have alignment on the on-prem/air-gapped fit: 

Summary of requirements we heard:
- Production inference will run in an air-gapped datacenter (no outbound internet).
- Preferred operational model: customer-managed hardware with Redwood Private control plane deployed via USB/media.
- Expected peak throughput: ~120 requests/minute, average sequence length ~512 tokens.
- RTO/RPO: will need guidance on maintenance windows and hardware upgrades with minimal downtime.

Open items / actions for Redwood:
1) Share hardware matrix and baseline rack spec for 8/16 GPU configs (attached).
2) Provide an offline installer and runbook for air-gapped installs (high-level stub attached).
3) Confirm upgrade path and offline ops process (how we do kernel/binary updates, hot-swap vs rolling reboots).
4) Align on support SLAs and optional on-site assistance for the first two upgrades.

Next steps I propose:
- Michael (solutions engineering) to outline recommended rack configuration and offline upgrade options — target ETA Wed 6/23.
- John / LegacyBank to share any internal constraints (power/cooling, maintenance windows, spare parts policy).
- Marissa to send a preliminary SOW + procurement checklist for procurement to review (I'll circulate a draft by Fri 6/25).

Attachments: onprem_hardware_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_onprem_requirements_v2.pdf (spec summary).

Are you available for a 30-minute follow-up next week to walk Michael through the SRE questions? I can do Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Thanks — Marissa

John / Marissa — following up with the technical details we discussed. Key notes below and attachments with more detail.

Power / cooling estimates (per-node, typical):
- 8x A100-style nodes: idle ~600W, peak ~1200W per node.
- 16x A100-style nodes (dense rack): plan for additional 10–15kW per rack for cooling.

Upgrade / maintenance model:
- Redwood Private supports rolling upgrades across replica sets for the inference service — binaries are staged on an offline media image. The typical upgrade pattern is: stage image -> validate on one canary host -> roll across remaining hosts with health checks.
- For model binary updates that touch KV-cache formats we recommend a brief per-host restart; this can be done in a rolling fashion to meet 2–4 hour monthly windows.

Hardware expansion:
- Adding GPUs to an existing chassis is supported only if the chassis and power budget were provisioned from day one; otherwise we recommend adding a new rack and resharding workloads to minimize risk.

Offline install & airgap notes (see attachments):
- airgap_installer_notes.txt: step-by-step USB install flow, signed image verification, and failback plan.
- hw_spec_16GPU_rack.pdf: rack-level BOM with part numbers and lead time estimates (typical 6–8 weeks for special order GPUs).

I'll link our internal runbook for the initial install: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/On-Prem+Airgap+Runbook

Attachments: hw_spec_16GPU_rack.pdf, airgap_installer_notes.txt

If you want, we can schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive with SRE next Tue. I can bring our infra architect to review the upgrade sequences and emergency rollback plan.

Cheers — Michael
